newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin transfers Russia Moskvich stake to Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin transfers Russia Moskvich stake to Moscow.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has issued a decree transferring 59.07 percent of shares in troubled carmaker AO Moskvich to the Moscow city government, the president's press service said on Wednesday.

But the decree says the Russian government and Moscow government must agree government support for restructuring the company. The Moscow government must also agree to pay the company's federal tax and penion fund arrears within two years.
Total company debts at the beginning of the year were 2.3 trillion roubles, the company has said.
Moscow will not have to pay fines accrued on the arrears.
Moskvich production was halted last year and company officials say that full production cannot begin again without financial backing. Moscow officials have promised aid earlier this year.
Moskvich is only Russia's seventh biggest carmaker, but is a major regional employer, with staff of 20,300 in 1995, according to the magazine Ekspert.
